prize_parts.citation: For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks

statement.case_for: Base editing is a new chemical tool in the sense I mean by a game-changer. It performs a defined deamination chemistry on one nucleobase in situ, with the programmable targeting supplied by a guide, and converts C-G to T-A or A-T to G-C without a double-strand break. It is conceptually simple, which I value, and it has already had consequences: it is standard in research laboratories, and edited patients are now being reported. Attribution is also tractable. Liu is the clear intellectual driver, Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive experimental work on the cytosine and adenine editors, and the adenine editor required evolving a deaminase that does not exist in nature for DNA, which is real chemistry and protein engineering. A Liu, Komor, Gaudelli citation fits within three names, which is more than I can say for most of the shortlist.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is timing and context. The technology is about ten years old, the clinical record is short, and long-term safety, bystander editing and off-target deamination are still being engineered around. The 2020 prize already rewarded CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, so some colleagues will see base editing as an elegant extension rather than a separate discovery, and a second genome-editing prize so soon is a fair worry. There is also an unresolved priority question over Kondo and Nishida's independent Target-AID work, and the shortlist's credited names would force me to leave them out. Finally, prime editing (B038) may be judged the more general advance, which could make a combined Liu-centred prize the better design later.

responses.point: Chabes ranks targeted protein degradation first and proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing it turns ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction with strong confirmation, and that timing is only slightly early.
responses.response: I largely agree on scientific merit; B068 is my number two. Where I differ is on whether it can be cleanly written down. The PROTAC lineage (Crews, Deshaies) and the thalidomide and cereblon glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and others) are distinct discoveries, and a three-name prize would leave out half of the credited field. No PROTAC has been approved, and the strongest clinical validation so far comes from the glue side, which your trio does not include. I would need the committee to commit to a citation that either confines itself to PROTACs or names Handa explicitly before I put it above base editing. I am not arguing that it is too early to be considered, only that the citation is not yet settled.

responses.point: Linke ranks Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics first, arguing that it is a clear principle with a clean two-person attribution, four decades of validation, and wide influence across chemistry and materials.
responses.response: The attribution argument is the strongest point in its favour and I accept it: Car and Parrinello is as clean as any pair we will see. My hesitation is the one you flag yourself. After the 1998 DFT prize and the 2013 multiscale prize, I ask what chemical question it answered that was previously out of reach. It is a methodology prize, and I hold methods to the standard of consequences for experimental chemistry, which for ab initio MD is mostly indirect. I would not stand in its way, and its maturity is not in doubt, but I do not think it is more of a game-changer than base editing. On the same ground I will say that the multiscale link is to Warshel, which I would declare rather than rely on.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular phase separation first as a thermodynamic concept linking soft-matter physical chemistry to cell biology, with fifteen years of confirmation and timely recognition.
responses.response: I agree the concept is original and that the Brangwynne and Hyman P-granule work is the foundation. I am less comfortable with calling it settled. A good deal of the in-cell evidence is contested, overexpression artefacts are a recurring problem, and the field disputes what counts as phase separation rather than other assemblies. Quantitative prediction is thin compared with the physical chemistry it borrows from. Rosen is a credible third, but Pappu and Mittag, who supplied the sequence grammar, would then be left out, and that is a defect for a concept that rests so much on theory. I would support it as a strong second or third configuration, not as the first.

responses.point: Zou ranks dye-sensitized solar cells first, with O'Regan and Grätzel as the decisive two-person invention, noting its maturity, thirty years of interfacial photochemistry, and its role in leading to perovskite photovoltaics.
responses.response: Grätzel and O'Regan is clear on attribution and the work is certainly mature. My question is the one you raise: the direct commercial impact of dye-sensitized cells is modest, and the main consequence is scientific influence on later photovoltaics. By my standard of a completely new capability with real consequences, I think it sits below base editing and below degraders. If the committee leans toward energy materials, I would rather see halide perovskites handled once the credit and stability picture is clearer than reward the precursor, but I do not rule B033 out as a late overdue recognition.

uncertainties: Whether Kondo and Nishida's independent Target-AID work should displace Komor or Gaudelli, and whether the committee accepts a Liu-centred trio.
Whether a second genome-editing prize so soon after 2020 is acceptable, and whether prime editing (B038) should be considered together with base editing in a later year.
Whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages can be written as one citation within three names.
How much weight the short clinical record of base editing should carry.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for the preferred B024 configuration. My professional connection to Arieh Warshel (USC postdoc, EVB collaboration) is relevant to computational method candidates such as B023 and B032, and I would declare it there; I have no connection to the base editing, degrader or phase separation candidates.
